subject: General Knowledge
topic: Famous quotes and slogans — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The rallying war cry 'Dilli Chalo' was used by which armed force to galvanise soldiers fighting for India's liberation during World War II?

options.option_text: Indian National Army (INA) led by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose
Hindustan Socialist Republican Army under Chandrashekhar Azad
Indian Independence League led by Rash Behari Bose in 1942
Quit India underground network coordinated by Aruna Asaf Ali

questions.explanation: 'Dilli Chalo' (March on Delhi) was the battle cry of the INA/Azad Hind Fauj under Subhash Chandra Bose, directing troops toward liberating India from the east during 1943–45. Rash Behari Bose is a distractor as he founded the Indian Independence League (the INA's political parent) but surrendered command to Subhash Chandra Bose; the HSRA under Azad was a pre-war domestic revolutionary outfit, not a World War II fighting force.

questions.stem: Which Prime Minister officially expanded the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' into a three-part national rallying call by adding 'Jai Vigyan' to it?

options.option_text: Rajiv Gandhi, while inaugurating technology missions in the 1980s
Atal Bihari Vajpayee, addressing scientists at a public event in 1998
P.V. Narasimha Rao, during the economic liberalisation era of 1991
Manmohan Singh, while unveiling the national innovation policy plan

questions.explanation: Atal Bihari Vajpayee added 'Jai Vigyan' to Lal Bahadur Shastri's original 1965 slogan in 1998, reflecting national pride after the Pokhran-II nuclear tests. Rajiv Gandhi is a common distractor given his emphasis on IT and technology, but he never formally extended this specific slogan; Narasimha Rao and Manmohan Singh are post-liberalisation leaders whose periods don't match the 1998 Vajpayee event.

questions.stem: The patriotic anthem 'Vande Mataram' appeared in print for the very first time as an embedded song within which Bengali literary work?

options.option_text: Durgeshnandini (1865), debut Bengali novel by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
Anandamath (1882), a nationalist novel by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
Ghare Baire (1916), a novel on nationalism written by Rabindranath Tagore
Rajmohan's Wife (1864), Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's first English novel

questions.explanation: 'Vande Mataram' was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and first published within his 1882 novel Anandamath, set against the Sanyasi Revolt. Durgeshnandini (1865) is Bankim's first novel but contains no such song. Ghare Baire by Tagore is a frequent distractor as it also deals with nationalism and the Swadeshi movement, but it is a wholly different author and era.

questions.stem: The reformist call 'Back to the Vedas' was the ideological cornerstone of which 19th-century socio-religious movement founded in India?

options.option_text: Brahmo Samaj, founded in Calcutta in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy
Prarthana Samaj, established in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang
Arya Samaj, founded in Bombay in 1875 by Swami Dayananda Saraswati
Ramakrishna Mission, founded in 1897 by Swami Vivekananda in Belur

questions.explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati's Arya Samaj (1875) was built entirely on the premise of Vedic authority, rejecting idol worship, caste rigidity, and non-Vedic accretions. Brahmo Samaj under Ram Mohan Roy is the most common distractor — it promoted monotheism and social reform but drew on multiple traditions including Christianity and Islam, and never used 'Back to the Vedas' as its slogan.

questions.stem: The historic call for 'Sampoorna Kranti' (Total Revolution) in 1974, which united opposition parties against Indira Gandhi's government, was given by which leader?

options.option_text: Ram Manohar Lohia, socialist leader who opposed Congress throughout the 1960s
Jayaprakash Narayan, Gandhian-socialist who led the Bihar student agitation
Morarji Desai, veteran Congressman who later led the Janata Party government
Charan Singh, the farmers' leader who later became Prime Minister in 1979

questions.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) gave the Sampoorna Kranti call in June 1974 during the Bihar student movement, demanding systemic change beyond mere government change. Morarji Desai is the top distractor since he was the most prominent senior opposition figure of that era and later became PM in 1977, but the ideological vision and the slogan itself belong to JP's Gandhian-socialist framework.

questions.stem: At the 105th Indian Science Congress in 2018, Prime Minister Narendra Modi added a fourth element to the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan Jai Vigyan'. What was this addition?

options.option_text: Jai Anveshan, honouring the spirit of exploration in modern science
Jai Anusandhan, saluting research as the engine of national progress
Jai Avishkar, celebrating invention as a cornerstone of India's future
Jai Vigyanik, recognising the individual contributions of India's scientists

questions.explanation: Modi coined 'Jai Anusandhan' (Hail Research) at the 105th Indian Science Congress held in Imphal in 2018, stressing that research and development must drive India's growth. 'Jai Avishkar' (invention) and 'Jai Anveshan' (exploration) are linguistically plausible Sanskrit-derived alternatives that examiners use as traps; 'Jai Vigyanik' shifts focus to the individual scientist rather than the act of inquiry, which is why it is wrong.

questions.stem: The resolution declaring 'Poorna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) as India's political goal — and designating 26 January as Independence Day — was passed at which Congress session?

options.option_text: Calcutta Congress Session of 1928, presided over by Motilal Nehru
Nagpur Congress Session of 1920, marking Mahatma Gandhi's rise to leadership
Lahore Congress Session of December 1929, presided by Jawaharlal Nehru
Karachi Congress Session of March 1931, presided by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

questions.explanation: The Lahore Session (December 1929), presided by Jawaharlal Nehru, formally adopted Poorna Swaraj and set 26 January 1930 as the first Independence Day celebration. The Calcutta Session of 1928 (Motilal Nehru's presidency) is the sharpest distractor — it passed the Nehru Report demanding Dominion Status, one step short of full independence; it is precisely this distinction that the two Nehrus (father vs. son, Dominion vs. Poorna Swaraj) that examiners test.
